case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated the 12th day of November, 2002 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 4012, 2876 of 1999, 1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. In these appeals, common question of law is involved and the same have been heard together and are disposed of by this single judgment.

2. These appeals, by leave, are from the common judgment and order dated the 6th and the 12th day of November, 2002 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.4012 and 2876 of 1999 and Writ Petition Nos.1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002 making the Rules Nisi absolute in the first two petitions and discharging the Rules Nisi in the last two writ petitions.

3. Writ Petition No.4012 of 1999 was filed by Mohammad Ali, respondent No.1 in Civil Appeal Nos. 45, 50 and 53 of 2005, Assistant Director (Metrology), Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institution (BSTI), impleading the appellant of Civil Appeal Nos.45 of 2005, 50 of 2005 and 53 of 2005 as respondent Nos. 3- 5 who were the Deputy Directors (Metrology),

4. In Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the writ - respondents to show cause as to why the impugned orders as contained in letter No. BSTI/Admin/77/98 (Part) 3023 dated 31.05.1999 (annexure-U to the writ petition) and letter No. BSTI/Admin/77/ 88/1553 dated 31.3.98 (annexure-M(2) to the writ petition) passed by writ-respondents Nos.1 and 2 (BSTI and its Deputy Director (Admin) holding current charge), promoting writ-respondent Nos. 3-5, superseding the writ-petitioner and regularizing the previous service "by the writ-respondent No. 3 in the development project of BST1 by a bridge in spite of break of service should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and were of no legal effect.

5. The case of the writ petitioner was that he passed B.Sc. (Hons) and M.Sc. in Physics from Rajshahi University in 1980 and 1982 respectively and secured 2nd Class. He was first appointed as examiner (Electrical) in Bangladesh Standard Institution (BSTI) vide appointment letter No. BDSI/Pro- 89/70 (Part) dated 22.5.1983. Subsequently the writ-petitioner was appointed as Inspector (Metrology) in BSI vide letter of appointment No. BDSI(Pro-89(part) dated 24.11.1983 and he joined the service of BSI in the said post on 28.11.1983, Writ-respondent No.3, Md. Khademul Islam (appellant in C.A. No. 45 of 2003) was appointed as Inspector (Metrology) in the development project of the BSTI on the same date and he jointed the service on 28.11.1983. Writ respondent No. 4, Shawkat Osman, and writ-respondent No.5, A.B.M. Mortuza Hussain, were also appointed as the Inspector (Metrology) in BSTI on 08.12.1983 and 15.12.1983 respectively. The writ-petitioner in recognition of his efficiency and meritorious service was promoted to the post of Senior Examiner, Class-1, (Grade IX) of the modified new scale of pay, 1985 in BSTI with effect from 04.09.1988. In 1989 the writ-petitioner was chosen to attend the training course in Metrology Liner Management Technicians Technicians / Industrial measurement Techniques Program held in West Germany for a period of one year from 02.10.1989 to 30.09.1990 and his entire period in training abroad was to be treated as on duty vide office Memo dated 21.08.1991. While the writ-petitioner was undergoing the aforesaid training in West Germany, writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 were promoted to the post of Assistant Director (Metrology) in the meeting held by the Selection Board on 09.07.1990 and, in fact, there was no viva-voice examination. In the same meeting, it was decided that the vacancy in the post of Assistant Director would be kept open for the writ-petitioner subject to an interview on his return. After his return from west Germany, the writ-petitioner made various representations to writ-respondent No.1, BSTI to consider his case of promotion. The writ-petitioner also drew the attention of writ-respondent No.1 to the fact that there was already a precedent created in this regard by promoting some officers during their training abroad on the basis of seniority and merit but without any success. Writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5, who were appointed to the post of Assistant Directors as per the decision taken in the meeting held by the Selection Board on 09.07.1990, were juniors to the writ-petitioner as they were appointed as Inspectors (Metrology) on 08.12.1983 and 15.12.1983 respectively and the writ-petitioner was appointed as Inspector (Metrology) on 24.11.1983. After the return of the writ-petitioner from his training abroad he was promoted as Assistant Director (Metrology) in the same scale and grade as Senior Examiner on 29.03.1992. He was later transferred to the post of Senior Examiner on 30.05.1994 with the same scale as the Assistant Director on the plea that he was temporarily promoted as the Assistant Director although it was not so mentioned in the letter of promotion dated 29.03.1992. The selection committee thereafter promoted the writ-petitioner as the Assistant Director on 14.08.1997, stating that the writ-petitioner was in current charge of the post of an Assistant Director before although it was not so. The writ-petitioner was awarded selection grade scale VII with retrospective effect from 10.01.1994 by the office order dated 31.12.1997. Writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 were also given selection grade and they were placed at serial 21 and 22 respectively. Writ-respondent No.3 was, however, not given the selection grade as he was in the development project of the BSTI and not in the Revenue Budget of the BSTI. Since the project in which writ-respondent No.3 was appointed as an Assistant Director on 16.11.1988 came to the end his service was terminated on 28.03.1994 with effect from 31.03.1994. Thereafter, writ-respondent No.3 applied for the post of Assistant Director in the BSTI afresh pursuant to an advertisement in that regard on 17.07.1994 and he was thus appointed as the Assistant Director in the BSTI afresh on 09.10.1994 after he was out of service for more than 6 months. In 1992 the BSTI prepared a provisional seniority list and circulated the same on 06.07.1992 wherein the writ-petitioner was placed at serial No.19 while writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 were placed at serial Nos.12 and 14 respectively. Since writ-respondent No.3 was in the project of the BSTI he was not placed in the said seniority list. The writ-petitioner raised objection to his placement in the provisional seniority list below writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 and prayed for correction by fixing his seniority over writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5, but without any success. Subsequently a combined seniority list was prepared by the office order dated 25.10.1998, but this time to the writ-petitioner was not only placed below writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 but he was even placed below writ-respondent No.3. The writ-petitioner, therefore, raised objection for being placed below writ-respondent Nos.3-5 as he was senior to them in service. While the writ-petitioner was continuing in making representations for placing him below writ - respondent No.3-5 in the combined seniority list, BSTI on 31.05.1999 promoted writ-respondent Nos.3-5 to the post of Deputy Director by superseding the writ-petitioner by the impugned office order dated 3.1.05.1999. The BSTI in order to facilitate the promotion of writ-respondent No.3 to the post of Deputy Director bridged up the gap of his service for more than 6 months for not being in the service either in any project of BSTI or in the BSTI itself; hence the writ-petitioner filed the writ petition having no other equally efficacious remedy provided by law.

6. Writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2(BSTI and its Deputy Director (Admin) current charge) appeared in the writ petition and contested the Rule Nisi by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the writ petitioner was appointed temporarily as an Inspector (Metrology) under a development project of the BSTI namely, "Implementation of Metric System and Strengthening of Bangladesh Standard Institution" on 28.11.83 and not in the BSTI itself. Since his service as Inspector in the BSTI was not regularized before 29.07.1997, his promotion from the post of Inspector to Senior Examiner, on 04.09.1988 was illegal. Accordingly the promotion of the writ-petitioner to the post of Assistant Director (Metrology) by office Memo dated 29.03.1992 was irregular and it was therefore subsequently cancelled by transferring him to his former lower post of Senior Examiner by office Memo dated 30.05.1995. Later the writ-petitioner got regular promotion to the post of Assistant Director (Metrology) on 14.08.1997. But even that promotion was illegal as he did not serve the mini-mum requisite period for 3 years as Senior Examiner after regularization of his service on 29.07.1997 as Inspector. The writ-petitioner therefore acquired eligibility for promotion to the post of Assistant Director on 28.07.2000 and not before that date. Accordingly the writ-petitioner was not eligible for selection grade scale and the selection grade was given to him by memo dated 31.12.1997. It was further contended that writ-respondent No.3 (appellant in C.A.Nos.45, 47, 48 and 49 of 2005) was first appointed on 28.11.1983 as Inspector (Metrology) in a project under the development budget of BSTI like the writ-petitioner. Writ-respondent No.3 later applied for the post of Assistant Director in another project under the development budget of the BSTI pursuant to an advertisement and was appointed as an Assistant Director on 16.11.1988. The tenure of the project ended on 31.04.1994, accordingly, the service of writ-respondent No.3 was terminated on that date. Subsequently the post of Assistant Director in the development project was transferred to the revenue budget and writ-respondent.No.3 was appointed to the said post on 09.10.1994 after having been selected in open competition with others. The termination of service of writ-respondent No.3 in the project as Assistant Director with the end of the project was illegal as he ought to have been allowed to be retained in service till he was appointed Assistant Director on 09.10.1994 in the revenue budget of the BSTI. Writ-respondent No.3 therefore, submitted an application to the authority on 06.11.1997 for bridging up the gap in the service for about 6(six) months between the date of termination of his service in the project on 28.03.1994 and the date of his regular application in the same post as Assistant Director on 09.10.1994 in the revenue budget of BSTI, BSTT thereupon by office order dated 31.03.1998 bridged up the said gap and therefore, there was continuity of his service. Writ-respondent No. 3 was accordingly promoted to the post of Deputy Director before the writ-petitioner by the impugned office order dated 31.05.1999 writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were appointed as inspector (Metrology) and because of their satisfactory service record they were promoted to the post of Assistant Director and the Deputy Director on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.

7. Writ-respondent Nos. 3 and 5 also appeared in the writ petition and contested the Rule Nisi by filing separate affidavit-in-opposition denying the material statement made in the writ petition.

8. The case of writ-respondent No.3 (appellant in C.A.Nos.45, 47, 48 and 49 of 2005) was that the writ-petitioner as well as writ-respondent Nos.3, 4 and 5 were all appointed as Inspector (Metrology) in the development project of the BSTI known as "Introduction of Metric Systems of Weights and Measurement in the Country and Strengthening of Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institution". The writ-petitioner was appointed on 28.11.1983, writ-respondent No.3 was also appointed on the same date i.e.28.11.1983 and writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 were appointed on 08.12.1983 and 15.02/1983 respectively. When writ-respondent No.3 was serving in the post of Inspector (metrology), BSTI advertised for filling up the post of assistant Director. Writ-respondent No.3 then resigned from his post as Inspector and applied for the post of Assistant Director in the project afresh. He was thus appointed as Assistant Director in the project on 16.11.1988 and thereafter, he served as Assistant Director in the project on and from 16.11.1988 to 31.03.1994. Thereafter, writ-respondent No. 3 secured his appointment as the Assistant Director in the revenue budged of BSTI on 09.10.1994 through an open competition with others pursuant to the advertisement made in this regard by the BSTI. Since the writ-petitioner and writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 did not make any application for appointment to the post of Assistant Director in the revenue budged of the BSTI pursuant to the advertisement made on 17.07.1994, the promotion of the writ-petitioner as well as writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5 to the post of Assistant Director in the BSTI in 1992 and 1990 respectively was neither regular nor legal inasmuch as they were not entitled to be promoted to the post of Assistant Director in the BSTI before the post of Inspector in the BSTI was regularized after the said post of Inspector was transferred in the revenue budget of the BSTI, Accordingly, writ-respondent No.3 was senior to the writ-petitioner as well as to writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 as Assistant Director in the BSTI. The post of Assistant Director in the development project of BSTI was transferred to the Revenue Budget of BSTI vide Government Order No. Shim/ Sha/89-148 dated 27.06.1994. The process of transferring this post from the development budget to the revenue budget of BSTI took time and meanwhile the project ended on 31.03.19994. Accordingly, the service of writ-respondent No.3 as Assistant Director in the project was terminated and this termination of his service was illegal and violative of the Government circular dated 11.01.1992. Hence, writ-respondent No.3 submitted an application on 16.11.1997 to the concerned authority for bridging up the gap of service for more than 6 months with effect from the date of termination of his service on 28.03.19994 till his regular appointment as Assistant Director on 09.10.1994 in the revenue budget of the BSTI. The BSTI then bridged up the gap in his service by office order No. BSTI/Admin/74/88/9553 dated 31.03.1998. In this view of the view of the matter, the service of writ-respondent No.3 as Assistant Director in the revenue budget of the BSTI was and still is liable to be counted from 16.11.1988, i.e. from the date writ-respondent No.3 jointed the post of Assistant Director in the project of the BSTI. Hence, the promotion of writ-respondent No.3 to the post of Deputy Director (Metrology) by the impugned office Memo dated 31.05.1999 was legal and in accordance with the provision of BSTI Service Regulations 1989. One is required to be permanent class-1 officer in order to become eligible for selection grade of taka 4100-6500. Since the writ petitioner was not regularized in the post of inspector in the Revenue Budget of the BSTI until 29.07.1997, he was not eligible for selection grade scale. Hence, the selection grade given to the writ-petitioner was illegal and without lawful authority.

9. Writ-respondent No.4 did not appear and contest the Rule Nisi.

10. The case of writ-respondent No.5 was that he, was promoted to the post of Assistant Director (Metrology) with effect from 02.10.1990 on the basis of system of promotion prevailing in the BSTI and in accordance with the provision of regulation 7 read with regulation 14 of the BSTI service regulations, 1989. Therefore, there was no question of superseding the writ-petitioner nor there was any violation of any procedure connected with the promotion of writ-respondent No.5 by the BSTI." Accordingly, writ-respondent No.5 was rightly placed at serial No.12 in the provisional seniority list as Assistant Director (Metrology) and he was also rightly placed at serial No.26 above the position of the writ-petitioner in the combined seniority list in view of the fact that he was promoted to the post of Assistant Director earlier than the writ-petitioner. In the circumstances, the promotion, of writ-respondent No.5 to the post of Deputy Director (Metrology) by the impugned order dated 31.05.1999 was rightly given and was not liable to be interfered with.

11. Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999 was filed by Md. Abu Hussein, respondent No.1 Civil Appeal No. 46, 47 and 51 of 2005, Assistant Director (Metrology), BSTI impleading the appellants Md. Shawkat Osman, Md. Khademul Islam, A.B.M Mortuja Hossain Shah, all Deputy Directors (Metrology) of BSTI and Md. Khalilur Rahman, Deputy Director (Admin) as respondent Nos. 6, 5, 7 and 8 respectively. In this writ petition (2876 of 1999), the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the writ-respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order as contained in letter No. BSTI/Admin-17/90(Part)/ 3024 and letter No. BSTI /Admin/17/90 (Part)/3023 both dated 31.05.1999 (annexure-M1, M2 to the writ petition) and Memo No. BSTI /Admin/17/93 (Part)1633 dated 21.04.1998 (annexure-M to the writ petition), issued by writ-respondent Nos. 3 and 4 (the Director and the Deputy Director (Admire), BSTI) promoting writ -respondent Nos. 5 - 8 to the post of Deputy Director superseding the writ-petitioner and "amending the writ-petitioner's approved selection grade scale dated 31.12.1997 should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and were of no legal effect and why the writ-respondent No.2 should not be directed to promote the writ-petitioner to the post of Deputy Director as he was senior to writ-respondent Nos. 5-8.

12. The case of writ-petitioner was that he passed Diploma-in-Mechanical Engineering in 1982. He was appointed as Senior Examiner (Measures) in Bangladesh Standard Institution (BSI) which was subsequently known as BSTI by a letter of appointment dated 22.05.83. He was thereafter promoted to the post of Assistant Director by office Memo dated 22.01.1991. Writ-respondent No.5, Md. Khademul Islam, on the other hand, was appointed as Inspector in the Development Project of BSTI on 28.11.1983 and he worked as such till 15.11.1988. Thereafter writ-respondent No.5 jointed as Assistant Director (Metrology) in a development project of BSTI and at the end of the project the concerned authority cancelled appointed of writ-respondent No.5 on 28.03.1994. Subsequently, writ-respondent No. 5 was given appointment as an Assistant Director (Metrology) in the revenue budget of BSTI on 09.10.1994 after he was out of service for more than 6(six) months from 28.03.1994 to 09.10.1994, his aforesaid gap of service of more than 6 months was illegally bridged up in violation of rule 3B of the Employees Transferred from Development Project to the post of Revenue Budget Regularization and Seniority Fixation Rules, 1995 and thereafter, he was promoted to the post of Deputy Director (Metrology) on 31.05.1999, superseding the writ petitioner who was senior to writ-respondent No.5 by more than 3 years. Further case of the writ-petitioner was that writ-respondent No.6 was appointed as Inspector (Metrology) in BSI violating the terms and conditions of appointment as per the advertisement dated 08.09.1983 published in the daily Bangladesh Observer in that writ-respondent No.6 was under-aged being 20 years at the time of appointment and the requisite age for the post was 23 to 30 years. Moreover, writ-respondent No.6 and 7 were given promotion to the post of Assistant Director by office order dated 08.10.1990 in violation of the I3STI Service Regulations; 1989 as their seniority and ACR were not taken into account while giving them, promotion by resorting to 'pick and choose policy'. Writ-respondent No.8 was appointed as Co-ordination Officer in the BSTI on Ad-hoc basis on 23.04.1990. Although rule 5 of the Regularization of Ad-hoc Employees Appointment Rules, 1994 provides that a seniority of an incumbent shall be determined from the date of regularization of his Ad-hoc appointment the seniority of writ- respondent No.8 was determined not from the date of regularization of his service but from the date of his Ad-hoc appointment on 28.04.1990 in violation of the aforesaid rule. Accordingly, the Audit Report dated 16.05.1999 of the BSTI took exception and pointed out this irregularity. In this background of the matte, BSTI illegally prepared a combined seniority list of its officers and employees and placed the writ-petitioner below writ-respondent Nos.6, 7 and 8. The writ-petitioner made various representations for correction of the aforesaid combined seniority list but without any success. The BSTI, however, in consideration of the brilliant service carrier and excellent ACR of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Director (Metrology) accorded him a grade scale of taka 4100-7100 with effect from 06.05.1995. The BSTI subsequently on 21.04.1998 most arbitrarily amended the date of the writ-petitioner's selection grade scale and gave the same date of selection grade to writ respondent No.8 from 06.05.1995 and the writ-petitioner's date of selection grade scale was given from 26.02.1998 which was initially given to writ-respondent No.8. Although the writ petitioner was senior to writ - respondent Nos. 5-8, BSTI illegally and with malafide intention amended the date of the writ petitioner's approved selection grade scale and promoted the writ-respondent No.5-8 to the post of Deputy Director with effect from 31.05.1999 superseding the writ-petitioner in violation of the BSTI Service Regulations 1989 and its schedule. The writ-petitioner made various representations against the aforesaid promotion and the undue amendment of the date of his approved selection grade scale but received no response from the BSTI; hence he filed the writ-petition, there being other equally efficacious remedy provided by law.

13. Writ Petitions Nos.1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002 were filed by Md. Khademul Islam, (writ-respondent No. 3 in Writ Petitioner No.4012 of 1999 and respondent No.5 in writ-Petition No.2876 of 1999), appellant in Civil Appeal Nos. 45, 47, 48 and 49 of 2005. In Writ Petition No.1948 of 2000, the Rule Nisi issued calling upon the writ-respondents to show cause Why the impugned decision as contained in Memo No. BSTI(Admin)-166-94-498(5) dated 29.07.1997 (annexure -U to the writ petition), in so far as it relates to regularization of service of writ-respondent Nos.6 and 7, Md. Abu Hossain and Mohammad Ali, respectively in the post of inspector with retrospective effect from 01.07.1986 and Memo No. BSTI (Admin) 17/93(Part-1)12070 dated 31.12.97 (annexure-O to the writ petition) in so far as it relates to giving selection grade to writ respondent Nos.6 and 7 with effect from 06.05.1995 and placement of writ-respondent Nos.6 and 7 at serial Nos.28 and 38 respectively in the combined seniority list as Assistant Director circulated under Memo No. BSTI (Admin) 396/98 582(6) dated 25.10.1998 (annexure-0 to the writ petition). Should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and were of no legal effect and why writ-respondent No. 2 should not be directed to cancel the impugned Memo dated 29.07.97 and 31.12.1997. it may he mentioned here that writ- respondent Nos. 6 and 7, namely, Md. Abu Hossain and Mohammad Ali against whom the Rule Nisi in the instant writ petition was issued were writ petitioners in Writ Petition Nos. 2876 of 1999 and 4012 of 1999 respectively.

14. In Writ Petition No, 2305 of 2002, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon writ-respondent Nos.1-5 to show cause as to why the order contained in the office Memo No. BSTI/Admin/17/90/1873 dated 22.01.1991 (annexure-J-1 to the writ-petition), issued under the signature of the Director General BSTI promoting writ-respondent No.5 Md. Abu Hossain (the petitioner in Writ Petition No.2876 of 1999) to the post of Assistant Director (Metrology) in BSTI should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and was of no legal effect.

15. The case of the writ- petitioner in Writ Petition Nos. 1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002 was same as contended by him in his affidavit-in-opposition filed in writ Petition No.4012 of 1999. The additional facts stated in Writ Petition No. 2305 of 2002 were that writ-respondent. No.5, Md. Abu Hossain was illegally appointed as Senior Examiner (Metrology) in BDSI on 22.05.1983, According to the advertisement published by BDSI, the upper age limit for the post of Senior Examiner (Measures) was 30 years. But respondent No.5 was more than 35 years of age at the time of submitting the application to the said post, so he was not eligible for the said post. The post of Senior Examiner (Measures) in which respondent No.5 was appointed was abolished by the Zaman Commission report and he was transferred to the post of Inspector, as aforesaid, in BDSI in a Development Project. The project was completed on 01.07.1986 and the posts of the project were transferred to the revenue budget by the Memo dated 24.08.1987 and although the post of respondent No.5 was transferred to the revenue budget, his service was not regularized at that time, The writ-petitioner (Khademul Islam) was appointed as Inspector on 28.11.1983 in a development project titled "Implementation of Metric Systems and Strengthening of the BIDS" and respondent No.5 was appointed on transfer in the said project as Inspector on 08.11.1983. Respondent No.5 Was promoted to the post of Assistant Director illegally and he joined the said post on 31.01.1991. His service as Inspector was not regularized till 28.07.1997. Without regular appointment in the feeder post, no one could be promoted to the higher post. Respondent No.5 became a regular Inspector in the revenue budget on 29.07.19997, Respondent No.5 was not regularized in the post of Inspector till 28.07.1997 and he was promoted to the post of Assistant Director in violation of the existing service rules for promotion as there is no provision for promotion to the post of Assistant Director before regularization in the post of Inspector in the revenue budget. After completion of the project, the service of respondent No.5 was automatically terminated and he was not provisionally appointed to the post of Inspector in the revenue budget till 23.07.1997. Respondent No. 5 was appointed as Inspector on 24.07.1997 vide Memo No. BSTI/Admin- 17/90(Part)/ 497(14) and regularized as Inspector on 29.07.1997 vide Memo No. BSTI/Admin-166/94/48(5).Therefore, the promotion of respondent No.5 to the post of Assistant Director on 22.01.1991 was without lawful authority.

16. A Division Bench hearing all the writ petitions together by a common judgment and order dated 6.11.2002 and 12.11.2002 made the Rules Nisi absolute in Writ Petition Nos.4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999 and discharged the Rules Nisi issued in Writ Petition Nos. 1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002.

17. Against the impugned judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No.4012 of 1999 (this writ petition was filed by Mohammad Ali), Md. Khademul Islam who was writ-respondent No.3, Shawkat Osman who was writ-respondent No. 4 and A.B.M. Mortaza Hossain Shah who was writ-respondent No.5 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 659 of 2003, 695 of 2003 and 813 of 2003 respectively. Against the judgment passed n Writ Petition No.305 of 202 and in Writ Petition No.1948 of 2000. Khademul Islam filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.662 of 2002 and 663 of 2003. Against the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999, Khademul Islam, Mortaza Hossain, Shawkat Osman and Khalilur Rahman who were writ-respondent Nos.5,7,6 and 8 respectively filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.661 of 2003, 810 of 2003, 696 of 2003 and 660 of 2003. All these petitions were heard together and leave was granted giving rise to these civil appeals.

18. Leave was granted to consider the sub-missions made on behalf of the appellant in Civil Appeal Nos. 45,47, 48 and 49 of 2005 (in all these appeals, Khademul Islam is the appellant), whether the High Court Division was correct in holding that the writ-petitioners of Writ Petition Nos. 4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999 were senior to Khademul Islam in the post of the Assistant Director (Khademul Islam was the petitioner in Writ Petition No.2305 and 1948 of 2000); whether the High Court Division was correct the holding that bridging the gap of service of Khademul Islam from 28.03.1994 to 09.10.1994 was illegal; whether the High Court Division was correct in holding that the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Abu Hossain, were appointed as Inspector in the revenue budget and not in the development project; whether the promotion of Khademul Islam to the post of Deputy Director was given superseding the writ-petitioners; whether the writ-respondents, Shawkat Osman and A.B.M. Mourtaza Hossain Shah were junior to the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Abu Hossain and whether they were promoted as the Assistant Director and the Deputy Directors superseding the writ-petitioners; whether the writ-petitioners. Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain were illegally promoted to the post of Assistant Director provisionally though there was no substantive vacancy in the post of Assistant Director without the recommendation of the Selection Board of BSTI; whether the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain had any locus stand to challenge the regularization of writ -respondent No.8, Khalilur Rahman, a Co-ordination officer, whether Khalilur Rahman was promoted to the post of the Deputy Director (Administration) superseding the writ-petitioners counting his seniority from the date of his ad-hoc appointment; whether the writ-petitioners were illegally placed in the combined gradation list below the writ-respondents, namely, Khademul Islam, Shawkat Osman and Mortuza Hossain and whether the BSTI acted illegally in amending the date of selection grade of writ-petitioner, Md. Abu Hossain from 06.05.1995 to 21.04.1998 and the date of selection grade of writ-respondent No.8, Khalilur Rahman from 21.04.1998 to 06.05.1995, inasmuch as writ-respondent No.8 was regularized as Co-ordination Officer on 09.11.1992 with effect from 09.12.1990 upon the recommendation of the Selection Board prior to the coming into force of the Rules of 1994 and further writ-respondent No.8 was originally appointed in the Revenue budget and so he was legally regularized with effect from the date of his appointment in the Revenue budget and the writ-petitioner did not challenge the regularization of respondent No.8 for 7 years not even in the writ petition: whether the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering the fact that respondent No.8 was appointed as a Class officer in the post of Co-ordination Officer on 09.12.1990.

19. Heard Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Advocate for the appellants in Civil Appeal Nos.45 and 47-49 of 2005, Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Advocate for the appellant in Civil Appeal No.46 of 2006, Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate for the appellants in Civil Appeal No.50-53 of 2005, Mr. Shafique Ahmed, learned Advocate for respondent No.1 in all the appeals, Mr. A.F. Hassan Arif, learned Advocate for respondent No.3 in Civil Appeal Nos.45 and 46 of 2005, Mr. Firoz Shah, learned Advocate-on-Record for respondent No.3 in Civil Appeal Nos.47, 48 of 2005, for respondent No.4 in Civil Appeal No.49 of 2005, for respondent No.3 in Civil Appeal Nos.50, 51,52 and 53 of 2005.

20. At the very outset, it is to be mentioned that in the meantime, Md. Abu Hossain who filed Writ Petition No.2876 of 1999 died and Mohammad Ali who filed Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 went on LPR.

21. The High Court Division made the Rules Nisi absolute in these two writ petitions. It may be further stated that Writ Petition Nos. 1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2000 were filed by Md. Khademul Islam, appellant in C.A.Nos.45, 47, 48 and 19 of 2005.

22. As stated earlier; in Writ Petition No.4012 of 1999, Mohammad Ali challenged the orders as contained in Letter No. BSTI/ADMIN/77/98(Part)/3023 dated 31.05.1999 and Letter No. BSTI/ ADMIN/7/88/1553 dated 31.03.1998 passed by writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2 promoting writ-respondent Nos.3-5, namely, Khademul Islam (appellant in C.A.No.45 of 2005). writ-respondent No. 4 Md. Shawkat Osman (appellant in C.A.No.50 of 2005) and Mortuza Hossain (appellant in C.A.No.53 of 2005) (these three appeals have arisen out of the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.4012 of 1999) alleging that he was superseded in promoting them to the post of the Deputy Director, BSTI and that the previous service of writ-respondent No.3, Khademul Islam was illegally counted by bridging the gap from 28.03.1994 to 09.10.1994. In the writ-petition, the writ-petitioner also sought a direction upon writ -respondent No.1, namely, BSTI to consider his promotion to the post of the Deputy Director, Meteorology with seniority and also to publish the correct "grade wise seniority list" of the officers of Institution and placing his name above serial No.25 of the gradation list.

23. In Writ Petition No.2876 of 1999 filed by Md. Abu Hossain similar memos as challenged by Md. Mohammad Ali were impugned and he also challenged the amendment of his approved selection grade scale dated 31.12.1997 to have been made without lawful authority and was of no legal effect and for further direction upon writ respondent No.2, Director General, BSTI to promote him to the post of Deputy Director as he was allegedly senior to writ-respondent Nos.5-8 with the other similar direction upon the writ-respondents as prayed for by Mohammad Ali. In this writ petition, Md. Khademul Islam, Shawkat Osman, A.B.M. Mortuza Hussain Shah all, Deputy Directors (Metrology), BSTI were impleaded as writ-respondent Nos.5-7, Md. Khalilur Rahman, Deputy Director (Admin), BSTI, was impleaded as writ-respondent No.8 and they have filed Civil Appeal Nos.47, 52, 51 and 46 of 2005 respectively.

24. The High Court Division in making the Rules Nisi absolute in Writ Petition Nos.4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999 gave direction upon the BSTI to consider the case of Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain for promotion to the post of the Deputy Director. Though in the penultimate portion of the judgment, the High Court Division did not say specifically about the bridging of the gap of the service of Khademul Islam from 28.03.1994, in the body of the judgment gave specific finding that the bridging the gap in the service of Khademul Islam was illegal. The High Court Division also gave finding that all the writ-respondents, namely, Khademul Islam, Shawkat Osman, Mortuza Hossain and Khalilur Rahman were junior to the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain and they superseded the writ-petitioners in getting promotion to the post of the Deputy Director. The High Court Division also gave finding that regularization of the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain in their service with retrospective effect from 01.07.1986 was illegal and that they were entitled to count their seniority from the date of their appointment in 1983 and that the amendment of the date of selection grade of writ-petitioner, Md. Abu Hossain was also illegal.

25. In view of the prayers made in Writ Petition Nos.4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999, the terms of the Rule issued therein and the directions given in the impugned judgment, with the death of Md. Abu Hossain and retirement of Mohammad Ali, in fact, the second part of the penultimate ordering portion of the judgment has become infractuous (anfractuous). In the context, it is to be pointed out that in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999, Md. Khalilur Rahman was not made a party. So we shall confine ourselves to the first part of the prayer made in Writ-Petition Nos. 2305 of 1999 and 4012 of 1999 and the finding given by the High Court Division in that respect only.

26. In Writ Petition 2305 of 1999, the writ-petitioner, Khademul Islam challenged the office memorandum under reference BSTI/Administration-17/90/1873 dated 22.01.1991 issued under the signature of the Director General of BSTI promoting Md. Abu Hossain to the post of Assistant Director to have been declared without lawful authority and was of no legal effect. The maid ground for challenging the promotion of Md. Abu Hossain was that he was appointed in the revenue budget from the post of Inspector in the Development' project, namely, "Implementation of Metric Systems and Strengthening of Bangladesh Standards Institution" before regularization as Inspector in the revenue budget.

27. In Writ Petition No.1948 of 2000, Khademul Islam (appellant in C.A.No.49 of 2005) challenged the orders contained in Memo No. BSTI/Admin-1-66/94/498(5) dated 29.07.1997, as far as it relates to regularization of the service of writ-respondent Nos.6 and 7, namely, Md. Abu Hossain (the writ petitioner in Writ Petition No.2876 of 1999) and Mohammad Ali (the writ-petitioner in Writ Petition Nos.4012 of 1999) in the post of inspector with retrospective effect from 01.07.1986 issued by writ-respondent No.4, Deputy Director (Admin), BSTI and Memo No. BSTI/Admin-17/93(Part-1)/2070 dated 12.12.1997, so far as it relates to giving selection grade to the said writ-respondents with effect from 06.05.1995.and 10.01.1994 respectively issued by the said respondent and placing respondent Nos.6 and 7 in serial Nos.28 and 38 respectively in the combined seniority list as Assistant Director circulated under Memo No. BSTI/Admin-396/98/582/(6) dated 25.10.1998 issued by writ-respondent No. 5, Assistant Director (Admin), BSTI to have been issued without lawful authority and were of no legal effect and also for direction upon writ-respondent No. 2, namely, BSTI represented by its Director General to cancel the impugned Memo dated 29.07.1997, so far as it relates to writ-respondents Nos.6 and 7 and the impugned Memo dated 31.12.1997, so far as it relates to the said respondents and their placement in serial Nos.28 and 38 respectively in the combined seniority list.

28. We are of the view that the death of Md. Abu Hossain and the retirement of Mohammad Ali, the cause of action to maintain these two writ petitions (Writ Petition Nos.1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002 giving rise to Civil Appeal Nos. 48 and 49 of 2005 no more exists and, in fact, these two civil appeals (Civil Appeal Nos.48 and 49 of 2005) have become infructuous (anfractuous). and we shall discuss first the property of the decision of the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999 giving rise to Civil Appeal No.45 and 47 of 2005 that the bridging of the service of Khademul Islam for more than 6(six) months, i.e. from 28.03.1994 to 09.10.1994 was illegal as the same was not authorized or supported by any law.

29. From the admitted facts in the two writ petitions (Writ Petition Nos. 4012 and 2876 of 1999) filed by Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain, it appears that Khademul Islam was appointed as the Assistant Director (Metrology) in the project, namely, Establishment and strengthening of Bangladesh Standard Testing Institution " on 08.10.1988 and his service was terminated on 28.03.1994 with the end of the project and thereafter, on advertisement for appointment in the post of the Assistant Director in the revenue budget Khademul Islam applied and he was appointed in the revenue budget in the post of Assistant Director on 09.10.1994. It is very pertinent to state that Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain did not apply for the post of Assistant Director in the revenue budget and thus, in between the period of termination of the service of Khademul Islam as Assistant Director in the development budget and his appointment as the Assistant Director in the revenue budget on 09.10.1994, there was gap of more than 6(six) months and this gap was bridged by the Ministry of Industry as well as by the BSTI vide its Memo No. শিম.স্বম-৯/বিএসটিআই-৪/৯৮/৪২ dated 31.03.1998 under-Reference No. বিএসটিআই/প্র:-৭৪/৮৮/৯৫৫ respectively in the Memo of the Ministry of Industries, reference was made to a circular of the Ministry of Establishment dated 11.01.1992 which reads as follows:

(ঘ) সংস্থাপনে মন্ত্রনালয়ের ১১-১-৯২ তারিখের পরিপত্র নং-সম/আর-১/এস-১৬ ৯১-৩৯(২৫৩ এর (ঘ) এ স্পষ্টভাবে উল্লেখ আছে যে, উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে নিয়োজিত প্রার্থীদের প্রতিযোগিতামূলক পরীক্ষায় অংশগ্রহণ করে কৃতকার্য হয়ে নিয়মিত নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত হলে তাদের পুরাতন চাকরীকালকে পেনশন, ছুটি ইত্যাদির জন্য গননা করা এবং বেতন ও রক্ষা করা যাবে। এছাড়াও উক্ত স্থানান্তরিত পদে প্রকল্পের পদধারীদের চাকুরী নিয়মিতকরণের ক্ষেত্রে চাকুরী ধারাবাহিকতা অক্ষুন্ন থাকবে।

এমতাবস্থায় কার্যকর ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করার জন্য অনুরোধ জানানো যাচ্ছে।”

30. The office order of the BSTI reads as follows:

অফিস আদেশ

নিম্ন স্বাক্ষরকারী আদিষ্ট হইয়া বিএসটিআই বিভাগীয় মেট্রোলজী ইন্সপেক্টরেট, ঢাকা এর উপ-পরিচালক (চ:দ:) জনাব মোঃ খাদেমুল ইসলামকে তাহার ৬-১১-৯৭ ইং তারিখের আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে জানাইতেছি যে, শিল্প মন্ত্রনালয়ের পত্র নং-শিম/স্বস-১/বিএসটিআই-৪/৯৮/৪২ তারিখ ১৯-৩-৯৮ইং মোতাবেক তাহার প্রকল্পের চাকুরী হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রাপ্তির পর অত্র প্রতিষ্ঠানে পুনরায় নিয়মিত নিয়োগের মধ্যবর্তী সময়ের যোগসূত্র (ব্রীজ) স্থাপন করা হইল।”

<u>31. From the office order, it is apparent that the Ministry and the BSTI bridged the said gap of service of Khademul Islam in view of the circular issued by the Ministry of Establishment vide No. k; 16 91/09(250) dated 11.01.1992 and this circular has got the force of law (sec the case of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment -Vs-Shafiuddin Ahmed and 2 others, 50 DLR(AD)(1998) 27). So, we find nothing wrong in bridging the gap of the service of Khademul Islam for the period from 28.03.19994 and 09.10.1994, but the High Court Division totally failed to consider the said circular of the Ministry of Establishment and thus erred law in holding that bridging the gap of service of Khademul Islam was done illegally. The High Court Division also failed to consider that due to bridging of the gap of the service of Khademul Islam, he was much Senior to the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain. This will be clear from the fact that Mohammad Ali was appointed as the Assistant Director in the revenue budget on. 14.08.1997 after regularization of his service on 29.07.1997 and he joined the post on 17.08.1997. It may be stated that Mohammad Ali was promoted to the post of Assistant Director temporarily on 29.03.1992. Md. Abu Hossain was promoted in the post of Assistant Director on 22.01.1991. So appellant, Khademul Islam in Civil Appeal Nos. 45, 47, 48 and 49 of 2005, was senior to the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain, but the High Court Division failed to consider the said facts in line with the circular of the Ministry of Establishment dated 11.01.1992 in holding that they (the writ-petitioners) were senior to Khademul Islam.</u>

32. So far as the appellants, Mortuza Hossain in Civil Appeal No. 53 of 2005 and Shawkat Osman in Civil Appeal No. 50 of 2005 are concerned as per the own case of the writ-petitioners (Writ Petition Nos. 4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999), they (Mortuza Hossain and Shawkat Osman) were appointed in the post of Assistant Director on 08.10.1990 respectively whereas, the writ- petitioners were appointed as the Assistant Director on 29.03.1992 and 22.01.1991, so they were surely senior to the writ-respondents. It is very pertinent to state that the writ-petitioners did not challenge the appointment of these two appellants in the post of Assistant Director, so we do not see anything wrong in their promotion to the next post of the Deputy Director, they being senior in the post of the Assistant Director.

<u>33. So far as the appellants, Md. Khalilur Rahman in Civil Appeal No.46 of 2005 is concerned, it appears that he stood absolutely on a different footing inasmuch as he was appointed as a co-ordination officer on 09.12.1990 in the revenue budget and he was regularized in the said post on 09.11.1992 with effect from 09.12.1990 upon recommendation of the Selection Board and he was promoted as the Assistant Director (Administration) On 23.10.1994, a different wing of BSTI and the writ-petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain did not challenge the regularization of Khalilur Rahman. It may further be stated that in Writ Petition No.4012 of 1999, Khalilur Rahman was not made a party and though he was made a party in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999 filed by Md. Abu Hossain, but he failed to show Khalilur Rahman was junior to him.</u>

<u>34. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as stated hereinbefore, we conclude that none of the writ-respondents in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999, an 2876 of 1999, namely, Khademul Islam, Md. Shawkat Osman, A.M.B. Mortuza Hossain and Md. Khalilur Rahman were junior to writ petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md. Abu Hossain and none superseded them in getting promotion to the post of deputy Director, and we find merit in Civil Appeal Nos.45, 46, 47, 50, 51, 52 and 53 of 2005 and all these appeals are allowed and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division making the Rules absolutely in Writ-Petition Nos. 4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999 is set aside.</u>

35. Civil Appeal Nos.48 and 49 of 2005 are dismissed as being infractuous (anfractuous).

36. There will be no order as to cost.
